question: In July 2021, which state government passed a resolution supporting an ad hoc committee report that favoured the creation of a legislative council?
solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In July 2021, the West Bengal state government passed a resolution supporting an ad hoc committee report that favoured the creation of a legislative council.
 
• Legislative councils are a form of bicameral legislature in Indian states, similar to the Rajya Sabha at the national level.
 
• These councils function as the upper house in states that choose to have a bicameral legislature, providing a forum for more detailed scrutiny of legislation.
 
• The creation of a legislative council requires a resolution passed by the state legislature and subsequent approval by the Parliament of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• West Bengal previously had a legislative council, which was abolished in 1969.
 
• As per Article 169 of the Indian Constitution, the Parliament can create or abolish a legislative council in a state if the legislative assembly of that state passes a resolution to that effect by a majority of the total membership of the assembly and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of the assembly present and voting.
 
• Currently, a few Indian states such as Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh have legislative councils.
 
• The re-establishment of the legislative council in West Bengal is seen as a measure to provide more in-depth legislative review and representation.
